chunks: Al-Bazawfari from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abu Ayyub from Samaan said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a female slave who went to a group of people and claimed that she was free, so a man from them married her and she bore him a child. Then her master came to them and established proof among them that she was his slave, and the girl confirmed this. He said: 'She and her child are returned to her master, and it is upon the master to pay the father the value of the child on the day she returns to him.'
I said: 'If the father has no money to buy his son with?' He said: 'His father will strive to earn its price until he pays it and takes his son.'
I said: 'If the father refuses to strive for the price of his son?' He said: 'Then it is upon the Imam to ransom him, for the child of a free person is not enslaved.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a child born to a slave woman and a free man if the master claims her?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the status of 'Umm al-Walad' in cases of mistaken marriage, emphasizing that the child's freedom is tied to the father's status rather than the mother's. It establishes a financial mechanism where the master compensates the father, ensuring the child is not permanently enslaved, reflecting the Shia principle of 'asl al-ubuhah' (primacy of lineage). The hierarchy of payment—first the father, then the Imam—highlights the Imam's role as the ultimate guardian of justice in resolving such familial and property disputes.
